# Welcome {.unnumbered}

Welcome to the **3XG Workshop**: an introduction to R and data science,
developed for participants of the 3XG study at [VITO](https://www.vito.be/).

## About this workshop

This book is the companion material for a hands-on workshop that teaches the
basics of working with data in R. It is aimed at students and researchers
involved in the 3XG study who want to learn how to import, explore,
visualize, and communicate about their data using modern, reproducible
tools.

The workshop does not assume any prior programming experience. By the end
of it, you should be able to:

- Set up and use R and RStudio (or another R-friendly editor) for everyday
  data analysis.
- Import data from common file formats into R.
- Perform basic data wrangling and exploration.
- Create clear visualizations of your data.
- Organize your analysis in a reproducible way.

## Structure of this book

The book is organized as a small set of introductory chapters:

- **Introduction** — the goals of the workshop, the tools you'll need, and
  how the 3XG study fits into this training.
- **Workflow basics** — the fundamentals of working with R: running code,
  naming objects, and calling functions.
- **Data import** — how to bring your own (or example) data into R so you
  can start exploring it.

This is intentionally a starting point rather than a complete reference.
As the workshop grows, more chapters covering data transformation,
visualization, and reporting will be added.

## About VITO and the 3XG study

[VITO](https://www.vito.be/) (Flemish Institute for Technological Research)
carries out research in areas such as remote sensing, health, and
sustainable materials. The 3XG study is one of the research efforts
supported by VITO for which this workshop was created, to help participants
build the data science skills needed to work with study data confidently.

## Acknowledgements

The structure of this book was inspired by the excellent
[*R for Data Science*](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) (2nd edition) by Hadley
Wickham, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel, and Garrett Grolemund, which is released
under a [CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 license](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/3.0/us/).
Only the general book layout (chapter organization, build tooling) was
reused; all text in this book has been written specifically for the 3XG
workshop.
